summary: Full first-pass test of QwickAds Sales Manager (JWT Bearer auth). Backend: created pytest suite (55 tests) covering auth, meta, dashboards, lead CRUD/filters/pagination, duplicate detection, call logging, follow-ups, proposals, conversion, analytics, employee mgmt, templates, CSV import/export and role scoping — 54/55 pass. Frontend: verified admin + employee login (form and demo chips), admin dashboard/pipeline/analytics/employees/import/settings, reminders bell popover, employee dashboard, role scoping (17 leads for Rahul vs 34 for admin), admin route guards for employees, call-outcome modal (loss-reason gating + note + follow-up persisted), lead add + duplicate warning + 'Create anyway', lead detail (proposal ₹ calc, conversion + confetti/badge, activity timeline), follow-ups complete/reschedule, CSV import preview+commit, template save persistence, desktop and mobile logout. One HIGH mobile-navigation gap found and one backend authorization gap.

critical.issue: No ownership/authorization check — any authenticated employee can complete or reschedule another user's (or the admin's) follow-up. Reproduced: Rahul's token completed an admin-owned follow-up and got 200. Add can_access_lead()/assigned_to check like other endpoints.

minor.issue: Only requires get_current_user, so any employee can list all users (names, emails, roles). Should be admin-only or return a reduced set.
loss_reason is not validated against LOSS_REASONS (arbitrary strings accepted, e.g. 'budget'), which silently pollutes /api/analytics/loss-reasons.

Sort is only on created_at with no secondary tiebreaker; when concurrent writes/deletes happen the same lead can appear on page 1 and page 2 (observed once during parallel test run, ~1 in 2 parallel runs). Add a stable secondary sort key (e.g. id).
Accepts a raw dict body (no Pydantic model) and returns 200 even when emp_id does not exist (returns null instead of 404).
Returns 200 with null for a non-existent template id instead of 404.
Includes deactivated employees (role=employee, active=false) in the performance table; should filter active users.

ui_bugs.component: AppShell / mobile bottom nav + Profile page
ui_bugs.issue: On mobile viewport (390x844) an ADMIN has NO way to reach admin screens: bottom nav shows only Home/Leads/Calls/Follow-ups/Profile and the Profile page contains only 'Log out'. Pipeline, Proposals, Customers, Employees, Analytics, Import Leads and Settings are reachable only by typing the URL or on >=lg desktop width. Critical for a mobile-first product.

issues: Uses native browser date/time inputs (<Input type="date"|"time">) instead of the shadcn calendar/date-picker component — inconsistent look and poor mobile UX
End date does not auto-recalculate from Start + Days (Days=30 while End stayed at Start+1), so the stored campaign end_date is inconsistent with duration_days
Deactivated employees remain listed with an 'Inactive' badge but there is no way to reactivate them from the UI

action_items: Add ownership/authorization checks to POST /api/follow-ups/{id}/complete and /reschedule (employees must only touch their own follow-ups).
Expose admin navigation on mobile (add admin entries to the bottom nav 'More' sheet or to the Profile page) — currently admin-only pages are unreachable on mobile.
Restrict GET /api/employees to admins (or strip emails for employees).
Validate loss_reason against LOSS_REASONS and return 400 for unknown keys.
Add a stable secondary sort key to GET /api/leads pagination.
Return 404 from PATCH /api/employees/{id} and PUT /api/templates/{id} when the record does not exist.
Replace native date/time inputs with the shadcn date picker; auto-compute conversion End date from Start + Days.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/crm.py is 845 lines — split into modules (leads, calls, follow_ups, analytics, import) to stay under the 700-line guideline.
Follow-up mutation endpoints are the only lead-scoped endpoints missing the can_access_lead() guard — extract a shared dependency so scoping cannot be forgotten.
GET /api/employees leaks the full user directory to employees; role-gate it.
PATCH /api/employees and PUT /api/templates take untyped dict bodies — define Pydantic models for validation.
Frontend AppShell duplicates the nav item list for desktop sidebar and mobile bottom bar; derive both from one config so admin routes are never omitted on mobile.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all tested flows pass; 1 HIGH mobile navigation gap)

rca_of_the_issue: Follow-up authorization bug: complete_follow_up and reschedule_follow_up in /app/backend/crm.py (lines ~430-452) fetch the follow-up by id and mutate it without comparing fu['assigned_to'] to the caller, unlike lead endpoints which call can_access_lead(). Repro: login as rahul, POST /api/follow-ups/<admin_followup_id>/complete -> 200. Mitigation: reject with 403 when user role != admin and fu['assigned_to'] != user['id']. Mobile admin nav gap: the bottom-nav item list in the app shell is hard-coded to the 5 employee routes and the Profile page renders only the logout button, so adminOnly routes have no mobile entry point.
